name: Hadad
title: Edom's Adversary Against Solomon
summary: Hadad was an Edomite prince from the royal house of Edom who fled to Egypt as a child when Joab, David's commander, defeated the Edomites. He was welcomed by Pharaoh in Egypt and given a high position there. After David's death, he returned to become an adversary of King Solomon, as God's judgment on Solomon's apostasy.

keyEvents.title: Joab's Massacre in Edom
keyEvents.description: When David and his commander Joab defeated Edom, all the men of Edom were sought to be exterminated. The young Hadad fled with some of his father's servants.

keyEvents.title: Flight to Egypt
keyEvents.description: Hadad fled from Edom through Midian and Paran, and eventually reached Egypt where Pharaoh welcomed him and gave him a house, food, and land.

keyEvents.title: Favor with Pharaoh
keyEvents.description: Hadad found great favor with Pharaoh in Egypt, who gave him his own queen Takpenes' sister as a wife.

keyEvents.title: The Son Genubath is Born
keyEvents.description: Hadad's wife, the sister of Queen Takpenes, bore him a son named Genubath, who was raised in Pharaoh's house among Pharaoh's own sons.

keyEvents.title: Hadad Wishes to Return
keyEvents.description: When Hadad heard that David and Joab were dead, he asked Pharaoh for permission to return to his own land, even though Pharaoh tried to persuade him to stay.

keyEvents.title: God Raises Up Hadad as an Adversary of Solomon
keyEvents.description: As part of God's judgment on Solomon's idolatry, God raised up Hadad the Edomite as an adversary against Solomon. Hadad hated Israel and remained an enemy throughout all of Solomon's reign.
